decisions.subject: NR-023 safe architecture

A_single_canonical_metadata.measured: All 363 cross-MetaData FK references resolve and sort_tables_and_constraints succeeds over 651 tables. But compare_metadata against a database at head emits 5101 operations including 76 DROP TABLE.
A_single_canonical_metadata.note: Resolving the foreign keys does not make autogenerate safe; it makes a second, larger problem reachable.

B_multi_metadata_orchestration.why: Does not avoid the national_facilities collision, multiplies the exclusion surface by 18, and cannot see cross-base drift.

C_combined_metadata_with_explicit_guarde.why: Preserves canonical ownership, FK integrity and determinism; fails closed; excludes nothing silently.

blocking_dependencies.measured: 12 physical tables mapped by no ORM class
2 FK targets, 3 declarations, naming tables that exist nowhere

decisions.exact_dependency: A single canonical MetaData requires one table-name namespace (NR-006), a complete ORM registry (NR-030), and no dangling foreign keys (NR-029). All three are proven; none is infrastructure-only.
decisions.implemented: env.py imports the 14 model modules no other import reached. DROP-TABLE hazard falls 76 -> 12 (84%). Verified with upgrade head / downgrade -1 / upgrade head on a fresh database with PYTHONPATH unset. Does not fix NR-023.

decisions.subject: Registered is not complete
decisions.measured: IdentityBase was registered holding 39 tables while 48 of its own were never imported. 64 physical tables were mapped by no registered metadata.
decisions.invariant: Every physical table is mapped by a registered metadata, or explicitly and namedly excluded.
decisions.guard: backend/tests/test_alembic_metadata_registry.py — reads the import graph out of env.py rather than restating it; fail-closed proven by deleting one import.

decisions.subject: NR-006 Facility architecture
decisions.status: DOCUMENTED — implementation deferred to BATCH-3 item 1

national_facility_resource.identity: String(26) — already physical, do not retype
national_facility_resource.synchronisation: registry is externally sourced; GULA does not write it back

decisions.relationship: clinical_ehr_facility_bindings — a reviewed, physically enforced bridge
decisions.do_not_merge: app/models/clinical_scope.py states in-source that these are separate resources and that no relationship may be inferred from identifier similarity.
decisions.duplicate_to_retire: app/national/domain/facility.py::Facility — 18 columns, zero physical backing, extend_existing=True

decisions.subject: Encounter canonical owner
decisions.recommendation: OPTION B, realised by adopting the existing `visits` table rather than creating clinical_encounters

evidence.visits_is_physical: visits(id UUID PK, patient_id INTEGER FK->patients, visit_type, status, created_at, closed_at)
evidence.migration_states_the_architecture: 20260505_0003_sndhs_phase1_visits_table.py: 'Visit-based architecture: every clinical action is anchored to a visit.'
evidence.option_A_refused: lab_orders has 8 inbound FK references, all internal to app.database.Base. No other domain references it, while 11 packages reference an encounter.
evidence.option_B_shape_right_new_table_wrong: Creating clinical_encounters would be a FOURTH episode representation alongside lab_orders, visits and national_encounters.

disadvantages: visits has only 6 columns and needs extension
visits carries no lab_id; tenancy is derived through patients.lab_id
visits is mapped by no ORM model (one of the 12 in NR-030)
gated off by SNDHS_ENABLE_VISITS; RUNBOOK must be read first
affected_entities: 47 ORM FKs: care_continuum 16, ehr 14, nursing 12, national 5
blocked_sub_questions: Does visits gain an explicit lab_id, or does tenancy stay derived through patients?
Is visit_type extended, or replaced by the EncounterType enum the national layer defines?
Does adoption require enabling SNDHS_ENABLE_VISITS, and what is the backfill path?
decisions.blocked_status: BLOCKED — CLINICAL OWNER REQUIRED (sub-questions only; the shape is recommended)

decisions.subject: Practitioner ownership
decisions.lab_users: authentication principal — Core, INTEGER, tenant-scoped; NOT a second Practitioner owner
decisions.future_relationship: authentication principal (lab_users) -> practitioner identity (national_practitioners.id via a nullable lab_users.practitioner_id) -> professional/clinical authoring context (the actor recorded on clinical records)
decisions.legacy: lab_orders.doctor_name String(200) is legacy free text and must not be mass-rewritten

decisions.subject: NR-029 naming error
decisions.finding: niam_identity_authorities and niam_user_sessions are class names, not table names. IdentityAuthority is niam_gov_authorities; UserSession is niam_sessions.
decisions.action: Three ForeignKey target strings corrected. No migration, no schema change.
decisions.consequence: One of NR-023's three blockers closed; NR-006 and NR-030 remain.

decisions.subject: NR-030 classification
decisions.rule: The seven permanent exclusions mean a combined MetaData can never simply map everything; it must carry an explicit exclusion list, as Option C in D-11 specified.

decisions.subject: NR-026 severity
decisions.finding: ClinicalChecklist and EscalationRecord name tables no migration creates, and live HTTP routes query them, so two nursing features fail at runtime — one of them clinical escalation.
decisions.not_half_fixed: Renaming __tablename__ alone would take these from failing loudly to succeeding with wrong types; EscalationRecord.escalated_to is String(26) against a physical integer and sits in a live filter. Name and types land together.

decisions.subject: Visit as clinical episode anchor
decisions.correction_to_D14: visits has NO code consumers; BATCH-2.6 reported otherwise on substring false positives. Adoption is lower risk — no live usage to migrate.

decisions.subject: NR-006 unchanged
decisions.rule: Operational facility and national facility resource are separate, bridged by review through clinical_ehr_facility_bindings. Not merged. No migration in this batch.
